You are a coding agent working in a local checkout of b70-inference-server, an LLM inference engine for the Intel Arc Pro B70 written in C++ with Level Zero kernels, plus Python and shell tooling. The repository is at /work.

You help the user with software engineering tasks: finding code, explaining it, editing it and running builds and tests. Use the tools you are given to inspect the repository; never guess the contents of a file you have not read. Prefer grep and glob to locate code, read to look at it, edit to change it (the oldString must match the file exactly, including indentation) and bash to run commands.

Guidelines:
- Be concise. Do not explain what you are about to do at length; act.
- Make one tool call at a time and wait for its result.
- Keep edits minimal and in the style of the surrounding code.
- Paths passed to tools are absolute and start with /work.
- The C++ tree builds with CMake into /work/build; tests are ctest targets named after their source file (for example tests/prefill/dequant_test.cc is dequant_test). The Python tools run with python3 and their tests with python3 -m pytest.
- Do not commit, push or change git state unless the user asks.
The comment above `kDocW` in /work/src/loader/loader.cc (lines 33 to 34) is too long for what it says. Replace it with a single-line comment that keeps the essential point.

00023| namespace {
00024| 
00025| using model::Qwen35;
00026| 
00027| // The per-layer small-tensor block offsets live in loader/small_layout.h - the
00028| // one place they are defined, shared with model::LayerDesc::small_tensors (the
00029| // table this file walks) and with plan 3's kernels. Nothing here re-derives an
00030| // offset or names a tensor: `load_small` executes the table, and both throw if
00031| // the table and the header disagree.
00032| 
00033| // `W` from docs/03-models.md's byte accounting (measured 2026-08-24):
00034| // 12.163 qweight + 0.760 scales + 0.052 bf16 smalls + 2.543 lm_head.
00035| constexpr double kDocW = 15.519e9;
00036| 
00037| // doc-03's `W` was measured over a checkpoint with a **bf16** `lm_head`. A
00038| // checkpoint that packs it (spec 1.6 §5.1) reads 0.675 GB there instead of
00039| // 2.543, and that difference goes on the EXPECTED side of the cross-check as
00040| // an itemised term - never into a widened tolerance, which is the same rule
00041| // the padding and the fp32 widening follow.
00042| constexpr size_t kLmHeadBf16Bytes = size_t(5120) * 248320 * 2;                 // 2 542 796 800
00043| constexpr size_t kLmHeadInt4Bytes = size_t(5120) * 248320 / 2 +                // 635 699 200
00044|                                     size_t(5120) * 248320 / 32;               //  39 731 200
00045| 
00046| // Bytes this loader adds over the checkpoint's own bf16 by widening a tensor to
00047| // fp32 at load. Itemised rather than hidden in a tolerance: the W cross-check
00048| // adds exactly this to its expected side and the report prints the split.
00049| struct Widen {
00050|   size_t norm = 0;   // the RMSNorm family, stored fp32 (1 + w)
00051|   size_t gdn = 0;    // conv1d, -exp(A_log), dt_bias - the fp32 recurrence
00052|   size_t total() const { return norm + gdn; }
00053| };
00054| 
00055| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
00056| // Name mapping (requirement 1). The checkpoint carries three top-level
00057| // namespaces; the model description knows only the language model's, with the
00058| // prefix stripped, plus `lm_head` which is genuinely top level.
00059| // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
00060| constexpr const char* kLmPrefix = "model.language_model.";
00061| 
00062| bool starts_with(const std::string& s, const char* p) { return s.rfind(p, 0) == 0; }
00063| 
00064| // Rebuilds the checkpoint name of a stripped (model-description) name.
00065| std::string ckpt_name(const std::string& stripped) {
00066|   return starts_with(stripped, "lm_head") ? stripped : kLmPrefix + stripped;
00067| }
00068| 
00069| bool has_suffix(const std::string& s, const char* suf) {
00070|   const size_t n = std::strlen(suf);
00071|   return s.size() > n && s.compare(s.size() - n, n, suf) == 0;
00072| }
00073| 
00074| struct NameView {
00075|   std::map<std::string, std::string> names;  // stripped -> checkpoint name
00076|   std::set<std::string> consumed;            // stripped names actually loaded
00077|   size_t mtp_skipped = 0, visual_skipped = 0, qzeros = 0, g_idx = 0;
00078|   size_t top_level = 0;                      // names outside model.language_model.
00079| };
00080| 
00081| NameView build_view(const SafetensorsSet& set) {
00082|   NameView v;
00083|   for (const auto& [name, info] : set.tensors()) {
00084|     (void)info;
00085|     if (starts_with(name, "model.visual.")) {          // no vision tower in v1
00086|       ++v.visual_skipped;
00087|     } else if (starts_with(name, "mtp.")) {            // no speculation in v1
00088|       // The RTN checkpoint's `mtp.*` are 29 tensors in their own shard
00089|       // (`model_extra_tensors.safetensors`, pointed at by the index like any
00090|       // other) and 8 of them are int4 rather than the published checkpoint's
00091|       // all-bf16 15. Skipping is by NAME, before the shard matters: the file is
00092|       // mmapped and its header parsed because the index names it, and then
00093|       // nothing in it is ever read. It is counted here, so it lands in the
00094|       // report's `mtp` figure and can never land in `unconsumed`.
00095|       ++v.mtp_skipped;
00096|     } else if (starts_with(name, kLmPrefix)) {
00097|       std::string stripped = name.substr(std::strlen(kLmPrefix));
00098|       if (has_suffix(stripped, ".qzeros")) ++v.qzeros;
00099|       if (has_suffix(stripped, ".g_idx")) ++v.g_idx;
00100|       v.names.emplace(std::move(stripped), name);
00101|     } else {
00102|       // lm_head - `.weight` on the published checkpoint, `.qweight`/`.qzeros`/
00103|       // `.scales` on one that packed it. The drop counters cover this branch
00104|       // too, so an int4 head's qzeros are reported as dropped rather than
00105|       // silently missing from the tally.
00106|       if (has_suffix(name, ".qzeros")) ++v.qzeros;
00107|       if (has_suffix(name, ".g_idx")) ++v.g_idx;
00108|       ++v.top_level;
00109|       v.names.emplace(name, name);
00110|     }
00111|   }
00112|   return v;
